The depth goes back further than the rest of the record shows. My earliest years
were in C and low-level systems programming, the kind of technical complexity
many people never touch, and I taught myself Java on the job along the way. That
is where my instinct for how systems really work underneath the abstractions
comes from.

What came next was my longest run at any one company: five and a half years on
the engineering team of a flagship enterprise Java application server, through
four major releases. I built the developer tooling teams used to build on it,
work novel enough to earn a granted patent. When a rival's technology threatened
the company's position, I ran the technical evaluation of that product and helped
acquire and integrate it into the flagship, real due diligence on someone else's
codebase, and it was a large part of how the company regained its market lead. I
also co-authored a book on the messaging system underneath the platform. Two
decades of doing this seriously, not since it became fashionable.
